name: MITRE ATT&CK for Enterprise (v15.1)
description: Versioned MITRE ATT&CK Enterprise Matrix with Windows-focused endpoint detection taxonomy and sub-techniques.

tactics.name: Reconnaissance
tactics.description: Gathering information to plan future adversary operations.

tactics.name: Initial Access
tactics.description: Vectors used to gain an initial foothold within a network.

tactics.name: Execution
tactics.description: Techniques that result in adversary-controlled code running on a local or remote system.

tactics.name: Persistence
tactics.description: Techniques adversaries use to keep access across restarts, changed credentials, and other interruptions.

tactics.name: Privilege Escalation
tactics.description: Techniques used to gain higher-level permissions on a system or network.

tactics.name: Defense Evasion
tactics.description: Techniques used to avoid detection throughout their compromise.

tactics.name: Credential Access
tactics.description: Techniques for stealing credentials like account names and passwords.

tactics.name: Discovery
tactics.description: Techniques used to gain knowledge about the system and internal network.

tactics.name: Lateral Movement
tactics.description: Techniques used to enter and control remote systems on a network.

tactics.name: Collection
tactics.description: Techniques used to gather information of interest to the adversary's goal.

tactics.name: Command and Control
tactics.description: Techniques used to communicate with systems under their control within a victim network.

tactics.name: Exfiltration
tactics.description: Techniques used to steal data from your network.

tactics.name: Impact
tactics.description: Techniques used to disrupt availability or compromise integrity by manipulating business and operational processes.

techniques.name: Command and Scripting Interpreter
techniques.description: Adversaries may abuse command and script interpreters to execute commands, scripts, or binaries. These interfaces are powerful system administration tools that can run code interactively or in batch scripts.
techniques.detection_guidance: Monitor process creation events for command and script interpreter binaries such as powershell.exe, cmd.exe, and cscript.exe. Correlate with unusual parent processes, network connections, and command-line arguments.
techniques.windows_relevance: Standard attack vector on Windows endpoints. Highly prevalent in dropper and lateral movement chains.

techniques.name: Command and Scripting Interpreter: PowerShell
techniques.description: Adversaries may abuse PowerShell commands and scripts for execution. PowerShell is a powerful interactive command-line interface and scripting environment built into Windows operating systems.
techniques.detection_guidance: Enable and inspect PowerShell Script Block Logging (EID 4104), Module Logging (EID 4103), and process command-line arguments (e.g. -enc, -EncodedCommand, -ExecutionPolicy Bypass, -WindowStyle Hidden).
techniques.windows_relevance: Most abused native interpreter on Windows for in-memory execution, cradle downloads, and post-exploitation.

techniques.name: Command and Scripting Interpreter: Windows Command Shell
techniques.description: Adversaries may abuse cmd.exe to execute commands or batch scripts. cmd.exe is the default primary command-line interpreter on Windows systems.
techniques.detection_guidance: Monitor cmd.exe spawned by unexpected parent processes (e.g. browsers, Office applications, web servers) and unusual command strings like /c echo or piped commands.
techniques.windows_relevance: Universal interpreter on all Windows versions.

techniques.name: Scheduled Task/Job: Scheduled Task
techniques.description: Adversaries may abuse the Windows Task Scheduler to execute programs at system startup or on a scheduled basis for persistence, privilege escalation, or lateral movement.
techniques.detection_guidance: Monitor execution of schtasks.exe with parameters /create, /change, or /run. Inspect Windows Security Event Logs (EID 4698: A scheduled task was created). Watch registry paths under HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Schedule\TaskCache.
techniques.windows_relevance: Core Windows persistence and privilege escalation mechanism used by ransomware and APT actors.

techniques.name: Boot or Logon Autostart Execution: Registry Run Keys / Startup Folder
techniques.description: Adversaries may achieve persistence by adding a program to the Windows Registry run keys or startup folder, causing the program to be executed whenever a user logs in.
techniques.detection_guidance: Monitor modifications to registry keys HKLM\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run, HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run, and RunOnce. Monitor file creation in Startup folders.
techniques.windows_relevance: Classic autostart mechanism on Windows; frequently targeted by malware droppers.

techniques.name: System Binary Proxy Execution
techniques.description: Adversaries may bypass process and/or signature-based defenses by proxying execution of malicious code through signed, trusted Windows system binaries (Living off the Land Binaries / LOLBins).
techniques.detection_guidance: Monitor command lines and network activity of signed Windows binaries such as certutil.exe, mshta.exe, regsvr32.exe, rundll32.exe, and bitsadmin.exe.
techniques.windows_relevance: Primary method for evading application whitelisting and traditional antivirus.

techniques.name: System Binary Proxy Execution: Mshta
techniques.description: Adversaries may abuse mshta.exe to proxy execution of malicious .hta files or inline VBScript and JavaScript.
techniques.detection_guidance: Look for mshta.exe executing with http://, https://, or inline javascript:/vbscript: protocols.
techniques.windows_relevance: Bypasses browser sandboxes and script execution restrictions.

techniques.name: System Binary Proxy Execution: Regsvr32
techniques.description: Adversaries may abuse regsvr32.exe to proxy execution of malicious code, specifically Squiblydoo scriptlet (.sct) execution over the network to bypass AppLocker.
techniques.detection_guidance: Detect regsvr32.exe invoked with /s /u /i flags pointing to remote URL or unapproved .sct file with scrobj.dll.
techniques.windows_relevance: Classic Squiblydoo technique used for stealthy remote code execution.

techniques.name: System Binary Proxy Execution: Rundll32
techniques.description: Adversaries may abuse rundll32.exe to proxy execution of malicious DLL exports, inline JavaScript, or payload entry points.
techniques.detection_guidance: Monitor rundll32.exe loading DLLs from temporary or user-writable paths, ordinal-only exports (#1), or inline javascript: protocol syntax.
techniques.windows_relevance: Ubiquitously targeted LOLBin for launching DLL payloads.

techniques.name: System Binary Proxy Execution: Msiexec
techniques.description: Adversaries may abuse msiexec.exe to proxy execution of malicious installer packages or DLLs via remote URLs (/q /i http://...).
techniques.detection_guidance: Detect msiexec.exe downloading MSI packages over HTTP/HTTPS or spawned by suspicious parent processes.
techniques.windows_relevance: Executes with elevated privileges when configured with AlwaysInstallElevated.

techniques.name: Windows Management Instrumentation
techniques.description: Adversaries may abuse Windows Management Instrumentation (WMI / wmic.exe) to execute malicious commands, query endpoint status, or perform lateral movement.
techniques.detection_guidance: Detect wmic.exe invoked with process call create or shadowcopy delete commands. Monitor WMI event subscriptions.
techniques.windows_relevance: Core Windows management tool commonly used for reconnaissance and lateral movement.

techniques.name: Modify Registry
techniques.description: Adversaries may interact with the Windows Registry using reg.exe or APIs to hide configuration information, establish persistence, or impair security features.
techniques.detection_guidance: Monitor reg.exe add, import, or delete commands modifying sensitive keys under HKLM\Software or HKCU\Software.
techniques.windows_relevance: Abused in almost all Windows post-exploitation persistence workflows.

techniques.name: Hide Artifacts: Hidden Window
techniques.description: Adversaries may use hidden window attributes (-w hidden, -WindowStyle Hidden, /b) to suppress interactive GUI windows during stealthy script or tool execution.
techniques.detection_guidance: Inspect command-line arguments of powershell.exe, cmd.exe, and scripting hosts for window-hiding parameters.
techniques.windows_relevance: Standard evasion technique to prevent user discovery of running scripts.

techniques.name: Ingress Tool Transfer
techniques.description: Adversaries may transfer tools or other files from an external system into a compromised environment using native tools like certutil, bitsadmin, curl, or PowerShell download cradles.
techniques.detection_guidance: Monitor command lines containing remote URL parameters (-urlcache, Invoke-WebRequest, /transfer, curl) and unexpected outbound connections from system utilities.
techniques.windows_relevance: Essential stage for multi-stage payloads and downloading secondary tooling.

techniques.name: Application Layer Protocol
techniques.description: Adversaries may communicate using application layer protocols (HTTP, HTTPS, DNS) to blend C2 traffic with normal network activity and bypass network filters.
techniques.detection_guidance: Monitor non-browser processes initiating outbound web traffic (HTTP/HTTPS) or anomalous DNS query volumes from endpoint workstations.
techniques.windows_relevance: Primary command and control mechanism across modern enterprise Windows networks.

techniques.name: Application Layer Protocol: Web Protocols
techniques.description: Adversaries may communicate using application layer web protocols (HTTP/HTTPS) to blend C2 traffic with regular web browsing.
techniques.detection_guidance: Inspect outbound HTTP headers, beacons, and SSL certificate anomalies originating from non-standard executables.
techniques.windows_relevance: Standard protocol choice for Cobalt Strike, Metasploit, and custom C2 implants.

techniques.name: Impair Defenses
techniques.description: Adversaries may maliciously modify or disable security tools, logging mechanisms, or system protections to prevent detection of their activities.
techniques.detection_guidance: Detect attempts to stop or disable security services (WinDefend, EventLog, Sense) via sc.exe, net.exe, PowerShell Set-MpPreference, or registry key tampering.
techniques.windows_relevance: Critical pre-ransomware step; adversaries disable Defender and tampering protections before encrypting.

techniques.name: Impair Defenses: Disable or Modify Tools
techniques.description: Adversaries may disable or modify security tools (e.g. Windows Defender, Sysmon, EDR agents) to avoid detection of their tools and activities.
techniques.detection_guidance: Flag PowerShell commands like Set-MpPreference -DisableRealtimeMonitoring $true or taskkill targeting security agents.
techniques.windows_relevance: Routinely seen in ransomware playbooks (LockBit, BlackCat, Conti).

techniques.name: System Information Discovery
techniques.description: An adversary may attempt to get detailed information about the operating system and hardware, including version, patches, architecture, and system name.
techniques.detection_guidance: Monitor commands such as systeminfo.exe, wmic os get, hostname.exe, and Get-ComputerInfo executed by interactive or script parents.
techniques.windows_relevance: Standard initial situational awareness activity following endpoint compromise.

techniques.name: Account Discovery: Local Account
techniques.description: Adversaries may attempt to get a listing of local system accounts using native commands such as net user or whoami.
techniques.detection_guidance: Monitor execution of net.exe user, whoami.exe, and local SAM queries from non-administrative processes.
techniques.windows_relevance: Used for privilege verification and credential targeting.

techniques.name: Obfuscated Files or Information
techniques.description: Adversaries may attempt to make an executable or file difficult to discover or analyze by encrypting, encoding, or packing payloads.
techniques.detection_guidance: Monitor execution of binaries from unexpected paths (e.g. %TEMP%, %APPDATA%, Users\Public) and entropy analysis.
techniques.windows_relevance: Standard technique for staging droppers in temporary directories.

techniques.name: Masquerading
techniques.description: Adversaries may manipulate features of their artifacts to make them appear legitimate, such as matching names, metadata, or locations of legitimate system files.
techniques.detection_guidance: Compare file paths and Authenticode digital signatures against known Microsoft publishers. Unsigned binaries in System32 or disguised as svchost are high-fidelity indicators.
techniques.windows_relevance: Very common evasion technique on Windows systems.

techniques.name: Valid Accounts
techniques.description: Adversaries may obtain and abuse credentials of existing accounts as a means of gaining Initial Access, Persistence, Privilege Escalation, or Defense Evasion.
techniques.detection_guidance: Monitor for unexpected interactive logins or shell execution by restricted accounts (Guest, DefaultAccount).
techniques.windows_relevance: Abuse of built-in and service accounts on Windows.

techniques.name: User Execution: Malicious File
techniques.description: An adversary may rely upon a user opening a malicious file (Office document, ISO, LNK, archive) to trigger code execution.
techniques.detection_guidance: Correlate file download timestamps with subsequent process execution from temp/download directories.
techniques.windows_relevance: Primary entry point via phishing attachments.

techniques.name: Inhibit System Recovery
techniques.description: Adversaries may delete or remove built-in operating system recovery mechanisms, such as Windows Volume Shadow Copies or backup catalogs.
techniques.detection_guidance: Detect execution of vssadmin.exe delete shadows, bcdedit /set recoveryenabled no, or wbadmin delete catalog.
techniques.windows_relevance: Universal precursor to ransomware file encryption on Windows.

techniques.name: Process Injection
techniques.description: Adversaries may inject code into processes in order to evade process-based defenses and elevate privileges.
techniques.detection_guidance: Monitor API calls like CreateRemoteThread, VirtualAllocEx, WriteProcessMemory, and target processes like explorer.exe and svchost.exe.
techniques.windows_relevance: Standard memory evasion mechanism in Windows.

techniques.name: OS Credential Dumping
techniques.description: Adversaries may attempt to dump credentials from the local security authority subsystem service (LSASS) memory, SAM database, or LSA secrets.
techniques.detection_guidance: Monitor memory access handles to lsass.exe (Sysmon Event ID 10) or execution of mimikatz/procdump.
techniques.windows_relevance: Most critical credential access technique on Windows domains.

techniques.name: Drive-by Compromise
techniques.description: Adversaries may gain access to a system through a user visiting a website over the normal course of browsing.
techniques.detection_guidance: Monitor web browser child process creations (e.g. chrome.exe, msedge.exe spawning powershell.exe or cmd.exe).
techniques.windows_relevance: Initial exploitation vector where browser compromises spawn shell utilities.

techniques.name: Command and Scripting Interpreter: Visual Basic
techniques.description: Adversaries may abuse Visual Basic (VBScript) via cscript.exe or wscript.exe to execute malicious scripts.
techniques.detection_guidance: Detect wscript.exe or cscript.exe executing scripts from temporary folders or proxying scriptlet components.
techniques.windows_relevance: Frequently abused via phishing attachments delivering .vbs / .wsf files.

techniques.name: BITS Jobs
techniques.description: Adversaries may abuse BITS jobs using bitsadmin.exe or PowerShell Start-BitsTransfer to download remote files in the background.
techniques.detection_guidance: Detect bitsadmin.exe with /transfer or /download flags, or inspect Microsoft-Windows-Bits-Client operational logs.
techniques.windows_relevance: Native Windows service used to evade perimeter proxy and firewall logging.

techniques.name: Deobfuscate/Decode Files or Information
techniques.description: Adversaries may use certutil.exe -decode or custom utilities to unpack obfuscated files staged on the file system.
techniques.detection_guidance: Detect certutil.exe invoked with -decode or -decodehex flags.
techniques.windows_relevance: Very common second-stage dropper behavior on Windows endpoints.

techniques.name: Non-Standard Port
techniques.description: Adversaries may communicate using a protocol generally intended for a different port, or over uncommon ports like 4444, 1337, or 6667 to bypass basic port-based firewalls.
techniques.detection_guidance: Analyze network telemetry for unusual destination ports (e.g. 4444, 1337, 31337) and protocol mismatches.
techniques.windows_relevance: Reverse shells (Metasploit, Netcat, PowerShell) commonly bind or connect back over uncommon high ports.
